title: Choose Munshi's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Voucher Screen. Keep it, take my pick, adopt an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Voucher Screen
options.lineage: The keyboard-driven accounting screens Indian order staff stare at all day
options.thesis: The page is the entry screen the staff already knows, filling itself in while they watch.
materials: menu list with a yellow highlight bar
voucher form grid with tabular figures
options.viewport: A light voucher screen: the order text lands on the left, the Sales Order rows fill in on the right, a yellow bar walks down each line, and Approve is the highlighted menu item.
options.risk: Can read as affiliated with the accounting software itself; it translates the grammar with no logos or trade dress. It is also the staff's world more than the owner's.

raised.raise: Headlines pair Latin and Devanagari as billing, so the Hinglish voice is set in type, not just in words.
One marked line splits the page: before approval everything is pencil-grey draft, after it the entry is inked and final.
A strict state vocabulary on every line: matched, learned, flagged, approved, each with one colour and one icon.
One spot colour, reserved: red appears only where a person must act.

options.label: The Duplicate Bill Book
options.lineage: Carbon-copy bill and challan pads with printed serial numbers and rubber stamps
options.thesis: Every order is a handwritten top sheet whose carbon copy comes out clean and checked.
options.viewport: A bill-book page: the messy handwritten order on the pink top sheet, peeled back to reveal the clean blue-carbon copy beneath, stamped Checked.
options.risk: The warm paper ground sits close to the cream default the critique flagged; it has to commit to the pink carbon sheet and blue ink to escape it.

options.label: Painted Film Poster
options.thesis: Munshi billed like a blockbuster, with WhatsApp, calls and slips montaged around a giant hero.
options.viewport: A painted montage of order channels orbiting the product name.
options.case: Loses on both axes: owners know the posters but not as their trade, and spectacle hides the calm accuracy claim.
options.kept: Latin and Devanagari paired as billing type.
options.risk: Kitsch around a product that touches the books.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Drafts develop slowly and become permanent only past a marked point.
options.viewport: An order developing in the tray before it is fixed.
options.case: Holds the draft-then-commit idea, but the audience has no link to darkrooms and amber-on-dark breaks the light-background requirement.
options.kept: Preview before commit; irreversible past one marked line.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.thesis: Order traces glow and fade as Munshi learns.
options.viewport: A dark field of glowing order trails.
options.case: Dark, abstract, and unrelated to the trade; loses both axes.
options.kept: A strict state vocabulary per item.
options.risk: The dark ground breaks the light-background requirement.

options.label: Mid-century Magazine
options.thesis: A strict two-column editorial grid with one hidden mark per view.
options.case: Elegant but foreign to wholesalers; loses both axes.
options.risk: Reads as a design magazine, not a trade tool.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Orders cut and stacked like blocks.
options.case: Surreal and ungrounded for this audience; loses both axes.
options.kept: Every quantity carries its unit, in tabular figures.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: One giant letter morphing under a slider.
options.viewport: A giant glyph with a live axis readout.
options.case: No link to orders or the trade; loses both axes.
options.kept: Hierarchy by type scale alone, no ornament.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean B2B SaaS landing page, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, subtext, WhatsApp button, and a product screenshot on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other SaaS page by design.
